records.supported_name_scope: Skagit River is the supported representative downstream system identity for the complete five-feature selection. Distinct headward, tributary, reservoir and delta-component identities remain separate; no one-name scalar assignment is made.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected Canadian opening uses the Captain Grant Creek-side feeder and Skaist River approach to the Skagit. It then crosses the Ross–Diablo–Gorge chain and follows the Washington Skagit to the North Fork Skagit outlet in Skagit Bay. The southern selected branch approaches through Sloan Creek, North Fork Sauk and Sauk. The selection does not encompass the full Skagit basin, every natural headwater, the full Suiattle, or both delta forks.
records.region: Washington–British Columbia Cascades, from the Skaist-side Canadian headwaters through the Skagit reservoir chain and the Sauk branch to Skagit Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative identity for the connected selected group, not a uniform reach name or permission for product application.
records.completion_scope: All five complete selected features were read against original federal cartography: three mainstem pieces, both successive Sauk-side tributary pieces, the Canadian headward joining sequence, the complete Ross–Diablo–Gorge chain, the Sauk–Skagit junction and the selected North Fork Skagit coastal terminal. Four original raster views, private original crops and separate selected-path orientation material supplied the review. Assessment is generalized component/corridor correspondence, not pointwise fitting, source-vector acquisition, geometry revalidation or a contemporary channel survey.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component_name: Captain Grant Creek-side feeder / Skaist River corridor
naming_scope_details.initial_headward_scope: Connected northeastern feeder, northward creek elbow and southwestward Skaist approach to the upper Skagit. The exact headmost feeder name and local name-transition vertices remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.selected_tributary_scope: Fid 9417 and fid 9418 together form the selected Sloan Creek–North Fork Sauk–Sauk branch to the Skagit. They are two modeled fragments of this branch, not two separately named natural tributaries.
naming_scope_details.terminal_limit: Selected North Fork Skagit River coastal outlet. The South Fork Skagit route and all other delta distributaries are outside this selected terminal path.
excluded_inferences: No scalar name is assigned to every selected river, creek, reservoir or distributary component.
No legal or registry hydronym status, official river length, precise source or mouth, modern flow condition or local name-transition boundary is inferred.
No complete Skagit basin, South Fork Skagit course, Suiattle course or other unselected tributary is added.
No Canadian CGN/geogratis name-search record or stopped report/map was used.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The cached selection was used only to orient the ordinary component comparison. Generalized bends, braid rendering and reservoir centerlines do not demand pointwise agreement. No product, geometry, name or code changes were made.

geometry_summary.scope: The single selected mainstem feature, including its full retained headward-to-tidal corridor and displayed terminal extension.

records.supported_name_scope: Edisto River is supported as the representative system identity. The selected route contains separately named South Fork Edisto River, Edisto River and the South Edisto tidal setting. This finding does not assign one uniform hydronym to every part of the retained feature.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected headward route is the South Fork Edisto southeast of the Johnston area, not the North Fork or the McTier Creek tributary. It continues through the Aiken-area swamp corridor, past the Denmark and Bamberg setting, to the North Fork junction near Branchville. The combined Edisto continues southeast, receives Four Hole Swamp and turns south near Givhans, then passes into the tidally influenced lower Edisto and South Edisto complex west of Edisto Island. The connected North Edisto/Dawho arm lies to the east and is not substituted for the selected southward terminal setting.
records.region: South Carolina, United States: Johnston–Aiken South Fork, Branchville and Givhans Edisto corridor, and the South Edisto coastal setting west of Edisto Island.
records.completion_scope: Three successfully acquired and visually read original National Map raster views cover the entire retained corridor with overlaps through the Aiken and Branchville areas. The selected headward branch, intervening swamp corridors and junctions, southward lower trunk, and broad South Edisto terminal setting are established at generalized component scale. Independent state coastal cartography and NOAA prose distinguish the adjacent estuarine arms. No unresolved material connector remains. The strongly generalized displayed seaward extension is not an exact channel trace or surveyed mouth.

naming_scope_details.terminal_receiving_water: South Edisto tidal river and coastal complex, which drains toward St. Helena Sound; the rendered endpoint is not identified as the precise natural river mouth.
neighboring_distinctions: North Fork Edisto joins the selected South Fork near Branchville; the upstream North Fork is not the selected headward route.
McTier Creek and Shaw Creek enter the South Fork corridor and are not adopted as the feature’s representative name.
Four Hole Swamp joins the Edisto just above the southward Givhans bend; its northeastward route is not the selected continuation.
Dawho River and North Edisto form the eastern coastal connection, while the selected terminal setting is the South Edisto side west of Edisto Island.
The neighboring Ashepoo and Combahee/Coosaw coastal waterways are not adopted as continuations or aliases.
naming_scope_details.wetland_and_impoundment_assessment: Original cartography shows an extensive wetland and branching-channel corridor along the South Fork and Edisto, widening into tidal marshes and estuarine channels downstream. No material mainstem impoundment is identified in the selected route at the reviewed map scale. The independently read boating-guide prose describes a free-flowing system; nearby ponds and managed coastal water areas are not relabeled as selected through-route lakes.
naming_scope_details.unassigned: Exact headwater source point; legal name-transition locations; precise channels and banks within swamps or tidal reaches; exact natural mouth and tidal limit; a uniform name for the displayed seaward extension; formal registry and Korean-language names.
excluded_inferences: No uniform scalar name is assigned to the full modeled feature.
The 251.312 km value is retained model metadata, not an official river length.
A generalized coastal extension does not establish the natural mouth or authorize exact shoreline, navigation or hydrologic claims.
Current shellfish harvesting permissions and field conditions are not inferred from the source map.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Generalized component and corridor correspondence only; no pointwise fitting, geometry revalidation, channel rerouting or geometry edits.

records.supported_name_scope: Supported receiving-system identity, not an assertion that every selected reach or tributary is named Guayas.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Western Ecuador: eastern headward feeders and the Catarama/Caracol–Babahoyo trunk, Daule-Peripa and Daule, the Quevedo/Vinces chain, and a southeastern Chimbo–Yaguachi feeder converge toward the Guayas estuarine channel. The selected ending is internal to that broad channel, not established as the actual ocean mouth.
records.region: Guayas drainage, western Ecuador, including portions of Los Ríos, Guayas and their headward drainage settings.
records.completion_scope: All 12 retained features received source-based observations. Six retain genuine branch or reservoir-connector gaps; the broad receiving-system identity and several middle/lower corridors do not complete whole-network correspondence.

These are component-connection gaps rather than exact naming-boundary or pointwise-bank questions.

naming_scope_details.operator_report_context: Baba/Toachi inflows and Quevedo outflow are supported as regional operator context, not names for all selected upper feeders.
naming_scope_details.terminal_receiving_water: Guayas estuarine channel; no actual ocean-mouth vertex assigned.

records.supported_name_scope: No whole-route hydronym is established. Tunun'ngum Kuugaa is an unconfirmed regional naming lead only and is not assigned to the selected route.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Prince Albert Peninsula, Victoria Island: inland stream valleys and a western loop continue through connected lake and channel country into a broad braided inlet-head tract at Richard Collinson Inlet.
records.region: Prince Albert Peninsula, Victoria Island, Northwest Territories, Canada, toward Richard Collinson Inlet.
records.completion_scope: Independent federal cartography covers the complete generalized headward loop, lake-linked middle and braided coastal terminal. No genuine missing geographic connector remains. Unavailable optional hydronym-placement material does not leave a geographic-coverage gap.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The complete geographic corridor is supported but no readable source observation establishes a single hydronym for the entire selected feature. The regional name lead is not placed on the route from a catalogue title or parsed figure-label list.

naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Broad braided and marshy inlet-head setting; no exact distributary, bank, surveyed mouth point, tidal boundary or current flow state assigned.
naming_scope_details.optional_unavailable_map: NTS88-A/11 (2010) was optional naming evidence, not a prerequisite for geographic coverage already supplied by the independent basemap.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
